toolchain: Lean 4.28.0 official release (leanprover/lean4 v4.28.0, commit 7e01a1bf5c70fc6167d49c345d3bf80596e9a79b), binary unpacked from the GitHub release asset lean-4.28.0-linux.tar.zst (sha256 ceb3a3f844f7aebf63245e2b51c28d5b0ed38942c19f93cf3febd520302160bd); elan could not fetch it (release.lean-lang.org refused by the session's network policy; not retried), so the binary was run directly; matches formal_diss/lean-toolchain
dependencies: NONE (core Lean only; no mathlib, no lake project)
axioms_per_target: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound for all twelve targets (no sorryAx, no custom axioms, no native_decide)
audit_command: cat DissAggregation.lean DissAggregationAudit.lean > x.lean ; lean x.lean   (exit 0)
statement_fidelity_audit: T6, T8, T11 (t = 2) restated with the definitions written out by hand and closed by the certified theorems
T13 hypotheses instantiated at the frozen parameter values (nuF 1/20, nuR 1/80, tau 3/10, phi_plus 1/4, rho 1/500, chi 2/5) on a concrete six-trial history: satisfiable, conclusion obtained

kernel fidelity: `run` evaluated on that history under both boards equals, as exact rationals, a Python transcription of the generator's three update lines (market_generator.py 145-149): low board (123880422274729007/156250000000000000, 5551423149729007/6250000000000000), high board (97055597240378629/122070312500000000, 4335859459128629/4882812500000000)
necessity of phi_plus <= tau: explicit counterexample with phi_plus = 1 (the legitimacy order reverses on a win)
deviations_from_frozen_targets: T9 split into the identity (T9), the weak inequality (T9b) and the strict inequality used as the witness against mean sufficiency (T9c)
T15 (two-type association) added: it is the sign statement behind observable implication O2 and was not listed in the freeze
T13 is stated for phi_minus = 1 (the frozen value) and for outcome sequences in {0,1}; the initial states are allowed to be ordered rather than equal (weaker hypothesis, same conclusion)
scope_limits: algebra and order over Rat only. Two types for T8-T12 and T15 (general populations: the covariance identity is definitional; Jensen for T11 is analytic). T13 is pathwise for a GIVEN outcome sequence: it does not say that outcomes are equal across arms. Nothing stochastic or behavioural is certified; the conditional-independence step in O2 is analytic.
